core.text: **the perfect subjunctive (the 'have done' form: nescio quid fecerit; ne timueris = don't be afraid)** is the subjunctive (the form Latin uses for wishes, purposes and what someone tells someone to do) for something already completed when the main verb is present: *nesciō quid fēcerit* — I don't know what he did. Forms: perfect stem + *-erim, -eris, -erit, -erimus, -eritis, -erint*; passive: perfect participle + *sim, sīs, sit* (*captus sit*). *nē* + perfect subjunctive is a sharp 'don't': *nē timuerīs!* Latin name: *coniunctivus perfecti*.
English 'did' in a report: *I wonder why you didn't tell me*. The telling is earlier than the wondering; Latin marks that gap.
Present main verb + a finished action in the clause → perfect subjunctive. nē + perfect subjunctive = don't (like nōlī + infinitive).

invented.en: I ask what the boy said.

core.text: Same endings except the first singular (*-erim* against *-erō*). The job decides: *sī vēnerit, gaudēbō* looks ahead to a future event — the future perfect (the 'will have done' tense); *nesciō an vēnerit* reports a past one; *nē vēnerīs* forbids. Signals for the subjunctive: *nē*, or a question word after a verb of knowing or asking.

more.text: Also easy to confuse: two ways to say 'don't' — *nōlī* + infinitive (*nōlī timēre*), gentle and the usual one in prose; *nē* + perfect subjunctive (*nē timuerīs*), brisker. Both are orders, not wishes.

The learner's notes: the perfect subjunctive replaces the present whenever a sense of completion is needed; 2nd stem + *-eri-* + the plain endings *-m, -s, -t, -mus, -tis, -nt* (*cēperim*); passive from the 3rd stem + *sim, sīs, sit* (*captus sim*). It appears in wishes and 'might' statements, but mostly after causal *cum* and in indirect questions: *nōn possum exīre cum aliquis portam clauserit* (I cannot go out since someone has shut the gate); *dīc mihi quandō advēnerīs!*; *sciō quandō nātus sīs* (I know when you were born).

Ørberg's chapter 32: *Iūlius dubitat num magister Mārcum laudāverit* — the doubting is now, the praising was earlier; *pater dubitat num fīlius laudātus sit*; and the prohibition *nē dubitāverīs dē verbīs meīs!* Irregulars: *fuerim, potuerim, voluerim, ierim*. In the sequence of tenses the perfect subjunctive is the 'before' partner of the present subjunctive; after a past main verb its place is taken by the pluperfect subjunctive (Week 12).
